## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the routine calibration, verification, and
proper operation of Mettler Toledo analytical balances used in the EA
Program laboratory. Accurate mass measurements are fundamental to nearly
every quantitative laboratory procedure, including soil moisture
determination ([SOP-L41](SOP-L41-soil-moisture.qmd)), loss on ignition
([SOP-L50](SOP-L50-loss-on-ignition.qmd)), DNA extraction
([SOP-L80](SOP-L80-dna-extraction.qmd)), and chemical reagent
preparation. Regular calibration ensures that balance readings are
traceable to national standards and within acceptable tolerance for
analytical work [@harris2020; @mettler_basic2023].


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** All Mettler Toledo analytical balances (0.1 mg
  readability) and precision balances (0.01 g or 0.001 g readability)
  in the EA Program laboratory
- **Does not apply to:** Portable field balances, top-loading balances
  used only for rough weighing (greater than 1 g tolerance), or
  microbalances (0.001 mg readability) requiring specialized calibration
  procedures
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Ensure annual professional calibration is scheduled |
| Lab Manager       | Perform monthly verification checks, maintain calibration log |
| Trained Personnel | Perform daily checks before use, report malfunctions |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Calibration weights are dense metal objects; dropping
  them can cause injury to feet or damage to the balance pan. Handle
  with forceps only.
- **Chemical:** Some samples weighed on the balance may be hazardous.
  Refer to the relevant SOP for the material being weighed.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling calibration weights or chemical samples)
- [ ] Safety glasses (when weighing chemical reagents)

### Emergency Procedures

If a chemical spill occurs on or near the balance, clean the spill per
[SOP-L02 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L02-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
before resuming use. If the balance pan or draft shield is damaged,
remove the balance from service and contact the lab manager.

## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Balance Placement and Environment

Proper placement is essential for accurate weighing. The balance should
remain in the same location and should not be moved unless absolutely
necessary [@mettler_basic2023].

1. Place the balance on a dedicated anti-vibration table or stone slab,
   away from doors, windows, air vents, and foot traffic
2. Keep the balance away from direct sunlight and heat sources (ovens,
   hot plates), which cause thermal drift
3. Verify the balance is level using the built-in spirit level. Adjust
   the leveling feet until the bubble is centered.
4. Allow the balance to warm up for at least 30 minutes after being
   powered on before performing any measurements or calibration
   [@harris2020]

### 6.2 Internal Calibration (FACT/iSOCAL)

Most Mettler Toledo analytical balances are equipped with an internal
calibration function (Fully Automatic Calibration Technology, FACT, or
iSOCAL) that uses a built-in reference weight [@mettler_basic2023].

1. Ensure the balance is unloaded and the draft shield doors are closed
2. Press the internal calibration button or navigate to **Menu >
   Calibration > Internal Calibration** (exact path varies by model)
3. The balance will automatically perform the calibration sequence. Do
   not touch the balance, lean on the bench, or create air currents
   during this process.
4. When the display reads "Calibration Done" or returns to the weighing
   screen, record the date and result in the calibration log
5. If the internal calibration fails, repeat the process. If it fails
   again, remove the balance from service and contact the lab manager.

::: {.callout-note}
If the balance is set to automatic FACT mode, it will self-calibrate
whenever it detects a temperature change of 1.5 C or more. However,
manual internal calibration should still be performed monthly as part
of the verification schedule.
:::

### 6.3 External Calibration Verification (Monthly)

External verification uses traceable reference weights to confirm that
the balance is reading accurately across its range. This check does not
replace the annual professional calibration but provides ongoing
confidence in measurement quality [@aac_guide2019].

1. Perform an internal calibration first (Section 6.2)
2. Allow the balance to stabilize with an empty pan and closed draft
   shield. Tare to read 0.0000 g (for a 0.1 mg balance).
3. Using forceps, place the reference weights on the center of the pan
   one at a time, starting with the smallest. Record the displayed mass
   for each weight.
4. Test at a minimum of three points spanning the expected working range
   of the balance (e.g., low, mid, and high):

| Check Point | Reference Weight | Acceptance Criterion (analytical, 0.1 mg) |
|:------------|:-----------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Low         | 1 g              | Displayed value within +/- 0.5 mg of nominal |
| Mid         | 50 g             | Displayed value within +/- 0.5 mg of nominal |
| High        | 200 g            | Displayed value within +/- 1.0 mg of nominal |

5. If any reading falls outside the acceptance criterion, re-zero, repeat
   the measurement, and clean the pan and weight with a lint-free wipe.
   If the reading is still out of tolerance, perform an external
   calibration (Section 6.4) or remove the balance from service.
6. Record all results, the date, and the operator initials in the
   calibration log.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Always place weights in the center of the pan. Off-center loading
(corner loading) can introduce errors, especially on high-resolution
balances. Periodically test corner loading by placing a single weight
at each corner and comparing readings.
:::

### 6.4 External Calibration (As Needed)

If the internal calibration or monthly verification indicates the
balance is out of tolerance, perform a full external calibration using
a traceable reference weight.

1. Navigate to **Menu > Calibration > External Calibration**
2. When prompted, place the specified calibration weight (the balance
   will display the required mass, typically its full capacity or a
   specific test weight)
3. Place the weight on the center of the pan using forceps
4. Wait for the calibration to complete and record the result
5. Repeat the verification checks in Section 6.3 to confirm the balance
   is now within tolerance
6. *TBD -- confirm external calibration weight value for the specific
   Mettler model in the lab*

### 6.5 Annual Professional Calibration

1. Schedule an annual on-site calibration by a Mettler Toledo service
   technician or an ISO 17025-accredited calibration laboratory
2. The technician will perform a comprehensive calibration including
   linearity, eccentricity (corner loading), repeatability, and
   hysteresis tests
3. Retain the calibration certificate in the lab's quality records binder
4. *TBD -- record the current service contract details and contact
   information for scheduling*

### 6.6 Daily Use and Best Practices

Follow these practices every time you use the balance to ensure accurate
and reproducible results [@harris2020; @mettler_basic2023]:

1. Check that the balance is level before use
2. Close all draft shield doors before taring or reading a mass
3. Allow the reading to stabilize fully (stability indicator appears)
   before recording a value
4. Use appropriate weighing vessels (aluminum tins, ceramic crucibles,
   weighing paper, or glass vials depending on the application)
5. Tare the vessel before adding sample material
6. Handle objects with forceps, spatulas, or gloves; fingerprints add
   mass and oils that cause drift
7. Never place chemicals directly on the pan
8. Clean up any spills immediately with a lint-free wipe or brush
9. Leave the draft shield closed and the balance powered on between uses
   to maintain thermal equilibrium
10. Record the balance ID, date, and any anomalies in the lab notebook

### 6.7 Cleaning and Maintenance

1. Wipe the pan and interior of the draft shield with a lint-free wipe
   after each use
2. Use filtered compressed air to remove dust from hard-to-reach areas
   inside the weighing chamber
3. If the pan becomes stained or corroded, remove it and clean with mild
   soap and water; dry thoroughly before replacing
4. Do not use solvents to clean the draft shield (they may damage
   acrylic or glass)
5. Inspect the draft shield gaskets periodically for wear; replace if
   they no longer seal properly


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Internal calibration (FACT): at minimum monthly, or after any balance
  relocation or significant temperature change
- External verification with traceable weights: monthly, recorded in
  the calibration log
- Annual professional calibration: required; certificate on file
- Daily pre-use level check: required
- Acceptance tolerance for routine analytical work (0.1 mg readability):
  displayed value within +/- 0.5 mg of the nominal weight for loads up
  to 100 g, and within +/- 1.0 mg for loads above 100 g
- If tolerance is exceeded after re-calibration, tag the balance
  "OUT OF SERVICE" and notify the lab manager

### Calibration Log

Maintain a calibration log (paper binder or spreadsheet) with the
following columns:

| Date | Operator | Check Type | Weight Used (g) | Displayed Value (g) | Pass/Fail | Notes |
|:-----|:---------|:-----------|:----------------|:--------------------|:----------|:------|
|      |          |            |                 |                     |           |       |


## 8. Waste Disposal

No waste is generated by this procedure. Cleaning materials (Kimwipes)
can be disposed of in standard trash unless they contacted hazardous
chemicals, in which case follow
[SOP-L02](SOP-L02-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).

## 10. Training Record

Before using the analytical balance independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Observe a trained operator perform internal calibration and external
   verification
3. Demonstrate proper leveling, taring, weighing, and draft shield use
4. Successfully complete a verification check with reference weights
   under supervision
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Troubleshooting {.appendix}

| Symptom                          | Probable Cause                     | Corrective Action                          |
|:---------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Reading drifts continuously      | Air currents or vibration          | Close draft shield doors; check placement away from vents and traffic |
| Reading drifts slowly in one direction | Temperature change or warm sample | Allow balance to equilibrate; cool samples to room temperature before weighing |
| Balance does not tare to zero    | Residue on pan or overloaded tare  | Clean pan; remove vessel and re-tare       |
| Internal calibration fails       | Significant temperature change or mechanical issue | Allow 30 min warm-up; retry. If persistent, contact lab manager. |
| Displayed value differs from reference weight by more than tolerance | Calibration drift | Perform external calibration (Section 6.4). If still out, remove from service. |
| "Overload" message               | Sample exceeds balance capacity    | Use a balance with higher capacity         |
| Balance will not power on        | Power supply disconnected or fuse blown | Check power connection; contact lab manager |
| Unstable reading with small masses (less than 10 mg) | Static charge on sample or vessel | Use anti-static device or ionizer; ground yourself before weighing |
